title: A joint test found no clear monthly rainfall concentration change in 48 US states between 1951-1980 and 1996-2025
abstract: We tested whether a prior national mean null result hid a clear state change in monthly rainfall concentration. We used NOAA nClimDiv state means and an annual precipitation concentration index (PCI). A joint test used 19,999 synchronous five-year block samples and all 48 contiguous states. The global p value was 0.200. All 48 simultaneous 95% intervals included zero. The equal-state mean change was -0.068 PCI units, with limits of -0.211 to +0.074. One-year blocks, ten-year blocks and adjacent periods also gave no clear state change. A secondary test of differences from the national mean gave a Florida contrast, but this result did not hold with one-year blocks or adjacent periods. These data do not establish that concentration stayed constant. Wide limits, short eras, one product and state means limit inference. This extends the prior mean test with joint state inference. Code, computed annual indices, all main samples, an independent arithmetic audit and a figure are included.

display.caption: All state changes have simultaneous 95% limits that include zero. The national mean checks also have limits that include zero. Limits are conditional on the data product, selected eras and block assumptions.

citations.reason: Prior national mean and decomposition tests set this joint state question. We use the same source snapshot and eras. This is not independent confirmation.
Prior seasonal grouping result also notes that a national mean can hide regional changes. Our metric differs.
